dedupe_keys.name: twin ports intermodal freight terminal study duluth superior 2003

description: This study, led by Richard Stewart of the University of Wisconsin-Superior with Robert Eger and the Tioga Group for the Midwest Regional University Transportation Center and the Federal Highway Administration (2003), evaluates whether a rail-truck-marine intermodal freight terminal could be established in the Twin Ports of Duluth, Minnesota and Superior, Wisconsin. Coverage: regions in the US and Canada assessed for intermodal cargo; benchmarks of small terminals in Neenah and Green Bay (Wisconsin), Auburn (Maine), Mobile (Alabama) and a failed one at Thief River Falls (Minnesota); surveys of major shippers and third-party providers; Reebie Transearch freight flows between 66 Business Economic Areas and the Twin Ports; a roll-on roll-off feeder service with Thunder Bay, Ontario; and a review of local rail yards as sites. Comparable terminals operate with about 40 to 80 lifts a day, 12,000 to 24,000 a year; the 2001 data point to enough cargo for about 28,000 lifts a year, with 21% more outbound than inbound Tier 1 cargo. Format and access: a report PDF hosted by the Minnesota Department of Transportation. Licence and cost: free to read; no licence is stated. Caveats: the freight data are from 2001. The lift thresholds and flow balances can be used to size terminal nodes in multimodal freight network flow and capacity planning models. It relates to the Freight Analysis Framework and the rail-truck intermodal network resilience study in the catalogue.
